channel.title: Acme: Tech News
channel.description: Articles about software, publishing and the open web.

item.title: Spreaker adds interoperable podcast recommendations through RSS
item.description: Spreaker now supports the Podroll RSS tag, allowing publishers to recommend any podcast to listeners regardless of hosting platform. Creators can use the feed-level list to cross-promote their own shows, connect a network's catalog or point audiences toward independent programs they value.

item.title: Podcast Show London expands around video and the creator economy
item.description: The Podcast Show London says its May 2027 edition will add a video-focused stage, a Creator Economy Zone and a larger exhibition floor. The sixth annual gathering expects more than 500 speakers across over 180 sessions, reflecting how podcasting's audio and video businesses continue to merge.

item.title: New fund targets independent newsrooms in European news deserts
item.description: Sustainable Media for Democracy will provide grants and operational support to about 45 local, community and investigative outlets across Europe. The 24-month program has €1.625 million for direct awards of €5,000 to €60,000, with proposal calls opening in December.

item.title: WordPress 7.2 Beta 4 arrives for testing
item.description: WordPress released the fourth beta of version 7.2, continuing the testing cycle ahead of the planned Dec. 8 release. The project warns against using the beta on production sites and asks developers and site owners to test it in disposable environments and report regressions.

item.title: French audio study finds listening moves freely across platforms
item.description: An Audion-YouGov survey says 58% of French adults have started content on one platform and finished it on another, while YouTube leads digital-audio use. Podnews also reports a new Flightcast tool that automatically moves creators' YouTube video catalogs and future uploads to Spotify.

item.title: How newsrooms make election calls before every ballot is counted
item.description: Reuters explains how the Associated Press and Decision Desk HQ combine official results, reporting, historical patterns and statistical models to determine when a trailing candidate cannot catch up. Networks and newspapers layer on their own analysis as low trust in election reporting raises the cost of a premature call.

item.title: W3C restores the missing early years of the www-talk archive
item.description: W3C combined and repaired partial copies of www-talk messages from 1993 through February 1995, regenerated the web archive and preserved old links with redirects. The restored threads include early announcements of Mosaic, CGI, robots.txt, Apache, SSL, cookies and public-domain CERN web software.

item.title: W3C backs an open-source polyfill for the experimental WebMCP API
item.description: W3C's second Open Source Program pilot will publish a WebMCP polyfill on npm and track the evolving specification and Web Platform Tests. The project aims to improve early interoperability while browsers experiment with exposing structured web-app functions to compatible clients.

item.title: WPVibe passes 100,000 active WordPress installations
item.description: WPVibe grew from roughly 2,000 active installations in July to more than 100,000 in six months. The WordPress plugin lets compatible conversational clients manage self-hosted sites through MCP, and its creator says it now handles about five million tool calls daily.

item.title: Adam Curry's Daily Source Code archive returns with transcripts and chapters
item.description: Christopher Isene rebuilt the complete archive of Adam Curry's pioneering Daily Source Code podcast, restoring 863 episodes and adding transcripts and chapters. Podnews links the new site and revisits Steve Jobs's early podcasting demo featuring the show.

item.title: Vox launches its first app as it pursues direct reader relationships
item.description: Vox's first mobile app combines articles, podcasts and video in one feed as the publisher tries to deepen paid membership and reduce dependence on outside platforms. Video and podcasts remain free, while text stories and ad-free audio require a subscription.

item.title: WordPress 7.2 Beta 2 advances developer APIs and admin modernization
item.description: The second WordPress 7.2 beta adds refinements to the Abilities API, server-side DataViews and DataForm registration, REST API flexibility, admin asset loading and modern SVG icons. It is for testing only; the final release remains scheduled for December 8.

item.title: Firefox roadmap adds offline reading, local speech recognition and per-site VPN rules
item.description: Mozilla's updated Firefox roadmap pairs recent performance and mobile-tab improvements with planned offline reading, read-aloud pages, locally processed speech-to-text and per-site VPN controls. The browser team says the work is being developed in public with contributor feedback.

item.title: Independent Journalism Atlas maps the hidden 'springs' in news deserts
item.description: A new survey of 46 counties labeled news deserts found information still moving through small independent 'wells' and ad hoc 'springs,' including meeting livestreams, local sports channels and neighboring outlets. The Atlas argues that mapping these informal sources reveals coverage traditional newsroom counts miss.

item.title: Meta promises publisher consultation before disputed web-scraping terms
item.description: Meta says it will consult news-industry leaders before implementing commercial terms that could permit broad scraping of sites tied to business accounts, even if that requires another delay. A Norwegian court has meanwhile blocked the terms pending review, while publishers continue to demand binding safeguards.
